claims.statement: A narrated recording becomes a canvas explored in space, with every part linked back to its source video moment.
Displayed pixels come from real frames at known times; unobserved areas are never filled and different moments are never blended across text.
Primary case is a narrated product walkthrough over scrolling static content; lecture is second; general video is a research question.
Changed states sit to the right, frequent changes collapse into stacks, motion plays in place, returns are linked, narration sits near its visit, and large regions can be captured.
Fixed 1/5/10 second sampling intervals.
First version needs no browser instrumentation, cloud service, or new frontend stack; analysis is offline and on request.
The canvas must beat ordinary video and a change-selected storyboard on real tasks, or the simpler view wins.
The portable HTML viewer is the first surface; native SwiftUI waits for proven value.
process_session.py already embeds session data into viewer.html via write_viewer and uses ffmpeg/ffprobe.
Mark images and browser event offsets are not exact frame-exposure times; extract_frame discards actual output time.
No test suite or tracked sample recording; OpenCV is not installed locally; FFmpeg is.
The first canvas surface is the native Sessions window, not viewer.html.
Lead job: find content passed through faster than scrubbing; sole user is Byron.
First slice: tall column per scrolled page left to right; changes, returns, and motion are plain cards. Recordings under 5 minutes. Built on request.
First version includes copy/export of a column PNG and adding a review mark from canvas content; narration uses the existing now strip and inspector; continuation decided by personal use.
Current scrolling fragments into cards after limited stitching; improve continuity and explore better presentation.
Native CanvasKit, CanvasTool fixtures and SwiftUI integration exist. Local source confirms region-discovery gating, immediate run closure, and geometry checks that return with no columns.
Combine continuity repair and stable page layout. Process the whole screen automatically with very little correction; a web page with sidebar and header is the first success case.
Use stable pages and a compact visit ribbon. Select narration and full-video playback by the active visit, with other visits available. Group uncertain related fragments with visible gaps.
Show transient UI as small source-playback event markers and persistent edits as local before/after markers. Defer composite capture until real scrolling works.

shape.appetite: One coherent scope combines automatic continuity repair and stable page layout for personal recordings under five minutes. Defer composite capture until real scrolling works.
shape.problem: Ordinary video review hides how much content was traversed, where it changed, and what was said about it.

recommended_shape.summary: Automatic whole-screen processing builds stable pages with a compact visit ribbon, grouped uncertain fragments, local before/after edits, overlay event markers, and active-visit click-to-full-video.
provisional_choices: Exact region proposal and recovery mechanics
Minimum representation for page identity and visit poses

success_moves: Require automatic full-screen coverage in acceptance; use known crops only to diagnose failures.
Reuse the native CLI and deterministic fixtures before native review of a personal recording.
Try independent regions and bounded recovery before replacing the matcher.
Keep event inspection separate from geometry anchors to preserve edits and overlays.
Separate pixel contributors from visits so repeated content keeps correct narration.
Deliver small runnable steps within the combined reconstruction and stable-page scope.

first_proof.question: Can a whole-screen web page remain a useful stable surface through sidebar/header interference, slow scroll, an overlay, an edit, a return, and a true jump?
first_proof.artifact: Native directed fixtures plus a disposable representative personal recording, reviewed in the stable page layout.
first_proof.decision_rule: Require useful reconstructed coverage, no false joins or lost edits, distinct visit narration, correct full-video seeks, and explicit gaps. A manually supplied crop does not pass.

rabbit_holes: Composite capture before real scrolling works
Inline playback despite the retained full-video click behavior
Browser instrumentation without a measured need
A database or graph service for visits

milestones.title: A whole-screen page reconstructs automatically
milestones.outcome: Build without a crop produces a verified tall page beside fixed chrome.
milestones.proof: Automatic sidebar/header and narrow-pane fixtures: one column, initial >=90% registered observed area, p95 <=2 px, max <=4 px, zero false joins; controls and source regions pass. Canary: 2026-10-13_00-57-10 copy builds without crop and its docs pages read as columns between both sidebars.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Existing chronological canvas displays automatically discovered columns.
milestones.rollback: Revert tracking/build changes; video review remains available.
evidence: canvas-tool check (whole screen, analyzer gets no document box): 12/12 clips pass, including new desktop and desktop-narrow fixtures (menu bar, browser chrome, sticky header, detailed left nav, right rail with moving highlight and scrollbar, Dock, drifting pointer, clock tick). One column each, coverage 97.4% / 95.4%, p95 0 px, max 0 px, zero false joins, 10/10 source regions.

Scroll clips gain a positive coverage gate (>=90% of observed document area correctly placed in columns; cards don't count): scroll 96.0%, reversal 96.3%, jump 94.6%, header 97.6%, cursor-scroll 98.0%. --supplied-box and --storyboard modes also pass.

Canary 2026-10-13_00-57-10 (whole screen, no crop): baseline 57 items (32 columns, 25 cards) with columns spanning the sidebars; now 48 items (31 columns, 17 cards), developer-page columns at x 320..<1120 (the document only), longest 6,591 px over 66 patches. Remaining breaks inspected: nested code-block scroller, page navigations, in-page changes while still.
In-app: --build-canvas full built the canvas through the native app path (CanvasDocument v2, box = whole frame) and the Canvas stage displayed 31 columns / 18 cards.

milestones.title: Slow scrolling and interruptions preserve content
milestones.outcome: Continuous geometry retains overlays and persistent edits as local events.
milestones.proof: Fractional/overlay fixtures remain continuous; before/after pixels and times match truth; pointer negatives and jump refusals pass. Canary rerun shows no regression; then Stage 1 personal-use review decides whether Stage 2 starts.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Existing canvas shows local event/change markers without losing observations.
milestones.rollback: Revert the coherent schema and reader change; rebuild derived canvas; recording remains unchanged.
evidence: canvas-tool check: 15/15 clips pass from the whole screen, plus --supplied-box and --storyboard. New: slow-scroll (0.5 px then 1.5 px a frame; sub-pixel shift estimates keep it one column, coverage 91.4%, p95 0 px), overlay (dropdown open mid-scroll; one overlay event at its first frame, column continuous, coverage 97.6%), small-edit (checkbox ticked and digit changed while a pointer drifts; two edit events with before/after frames of different page states, no pointer edits).
Old edit clip now keeps one column with an edit event at the changed value (before frame shows A, after shows B); a column may mix page states only when an edit event says so.
Bounded recovery: a run that stops lining up stays open 1.5 s against its anchor; replayed frames start the next run when the view doesn't come back (jump, repeated and blank still refuse).

Canary 2026-10-13_00-57-10: 10 items (8 columns, 2 cards) from 48; columns inspected for false joins (none seen). 5 events: 4 overlays (a hovered chip, charts briefly changing on the docs home) and 1 pointer-arrival edit (known limitation).

App: dashed outline + badge per event; edits open a before/after popover with Show in Video for each; overlays play their moment. Verified by offscreen render (display asleep; live window capture unavailable).

history.change: Prior research (intent brief, Pro report, design, proof plan, review) moved from docs/research/video-to-canvas to sources/ and reconciled into a sleuth intent brief.
Reordered proof: storyboard first as baseline and fallback; synthetic ground-truth clips before real footage.
Four milestones with one new dependency (OpenCV) isolated in M2 and a go/no-go in M4.

Three question rounds moved the surface to the native Sessions window (Canvas stage mode), set scope to <5 min recordings on request, added column PNG export and mark-from-canvas, replaced timed comparison with personal-use judgment, and added an engine bake-off.

M1 built: CanvasKit (AVFoundation decode with exact PTS, storyboard tracker, canvas.json), canvas-tool fixtures/check, Canvas stage mode. Analyzer moved from planned Python/FFmpeg to Swift because the project Python is stdlib-only.

M2: bake-off chose the in-app row-profile estimator (100% exact, 3.9 ms/pair, ambiguity signal, no dependency) over Vision (99.7%, 416 px miss) and OpenCV (100%, 25 ms, 50 MB dep). Added sub-pixel-tolerant verification and sticky-sidebar cropping from real footage.
M3: columns in Canvas mode with a hover time badge; row-to-frame mapping check added to canvas-tool. Purpose-made scripted recordings not yet recorded; existing real sessions stood in.
M4: Copy Image / Export PNG on canvas items; M and S marks from the canvas through the existing review-mark path; region math in CanvasItem.sourceRegion, checked against fixture truth.

Collected only the second Pro response and original ZIP; verified 550 manifest entries. Updated intent and provisional shape. Marked prior plan stale. Prepared ten product questions. No application changes or experiments run.

Absorbed all ten answers. Automatic whole-screen analysis and stable pages are one scope. Retained full-video clicks; selected visit-aware narration, local changes, and overlay markers. Deferred composite capture. Rewrote intent and shape; prior plan remains stale.

Replaced the obsolete implementation plan after questions 15–24. Preserved earlier implementation evidence here; M5 personal-use decision is absorbed into M9, not marked complete. No new implementation or native proof was run.
